## Observations

1. Adding an edge to a forest creates a cycle exactly when its endpoints are already connected.
2. At the end of the edge scan, every original edge has endpoints in the same kept component: either the edge was kept, or its endpoints were already connected when it was skipped. Thus the kept forest has the same connected components as the original graph.
3. A forest with \(N\) vertices and \(C\) connected components has \(N-C\) edges, since each component is a tree. Deleting edges cannot merge components, so no forest obtained by deletion can keep more than \(N-C\) edges when the original graph has \(C\) components.
4. A disjoint-set union structure can track connectivity without storing the edges. With path compression and union by size, each operation takes \(O(\alpha(N))\) amortized time, where \(\alpha\) is the inverse Ackermann function.

## Solution sketch

1. “A disjoint-set union structure can track connectivity without storing the edges. With path compression and union by size, each operation takes \(O(\alpha(N))\) amortized time, where \(\alpha\) is the inverse Ackermann function.” Read \(N\) and \(M\), initialize one set per vertex, and start a deletion counter at zero.
2. “Adding an edge to a forest creates a cycle exactly when its endpoints are already connected.” Read each edge in turn and find the representatives of its endpoints. If they differ, keep the edge and merge the sets. Otherwise, skip the edge and increment the deletion counter. This keeps the selected edges acyclic throughout.
3. “At the end of the edge scan, every original edge has endpoints in the same kept component: either the edge was kept, or its endpoints were already connected when it was skipped. Thus the kept forest has the same connected components as the original graph.” The scan therefore preserves connectivity within every original component, including isolated vertices, without needing a separate traversal.
4. “A forest with \(N\) vertices and \(C\) connected components has \(N-C\) edges, since each component is a tree. Deleting edges cannot merge components, so no forest obtained by deletion can keep more than \(N-C\) edges when the original graph has \(C\) components.” The kept forest reaches this bound, so print the deletion counter. It remains zero if there are no edges or if the graph is already a forest.
5. “A disjoint-set union structure can track connectivity without storing the edges. With path compression and union by size, each operation takes \(O(\alpha(N))\) amortized time, where \(\alpha\) is the inverse Ackermann function.” Initialization takes \(O(N)\) time, and scanning the edges takes \(O(M\alpha(N))\) amortized time. Reading one edge at a time gives \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
